title: DNA Confirms Woman Long Listed as 'Detained-Disappeared' Is Alive in Argentina, Triggering Fraud Probe and Search-List Review
detail: Chile's Servicio Médico Legal confirmed via DNA testing that a woman located living in Miramar, Argentina, is Bernarda Rosalba Vera Contardo — a teacher and MIR (Movimiento de Izquierda Revolucionaria) militant who has figured for more than 50 years on Chile's official list of detained-disappeared, after allegedly being detained and executed near the Toltén River in Panguipulli at age 27 in October 1973. Judge Álvaro Mesa Latorre, the minister overseeing the Human Rights case, informed Vera's family of the result on July 27, 2026, after comparing her genetic profile against family samples held in the SML's genetic bank for the detained-disappeared, which produced a match probability exceeding 99.9999%. Vera had in fact fled to Argentina after her 1973 detention, later gained Swedish residency (1978) and citizenship (1984), and returned to Argentina in 1999; her presence there first surfaced publicly in a September 2025 Chilevisión investigation. The revelation has triggered a criminal complaint over alleged fraudulent collection of state reparation benefits and pension payments by her family, with the case extended to examine potential administrative misconduct by former Justice Minister Luis Cordero and former Human Rights Program head Paulina Zamorano. Justice Minister Fernando Rabat said the government would review the official disappeared list to confirm 'que no contiene errores' (that it contains no errors) and refer the pension question to the State Defense Council.

media.caption: DNA testing confirms a woman found living in Argentina is Bernarda Vera, listed as detained-disappeared since 1973
